name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: US hits M/V Huda 7 Nov; tankers mined 8 Nov
summary: US disables a cargo ship on 7 Nov; Iran reports blasts at Qeshm and Jask and says two tankers hit mines on 8 Nov
state: CENTCOM said US forces struck the stern of the St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov after it refused to halt (India TV). Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and at Jask, cause unexplained, and Iran's military said on 8 Nov that two tankers caught fire after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz (ABC Australia). President Trump said on 6 Nov that US forces had carried out limited strikes on an Iranian air-defence system. Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals.
for_you: Merchant crews and shipping firms in the Gulf and Gulf of Oman are most directly exposed; UKMTO issues warnings for mariners. Travellers to the region can check FCDO travel advice. Energy and freight costs tend to follow events in the strait.
rubric_hit: Alert: active strikes between states and attacks on shipping, including the US strike on M/V Huda on 7 Nov and Iran's report of tankers hitting mines on 8 Nov.

sources.title: ABC News (Australia) — Explosions heard in Strait of Hormuz as Iran reviews de-escalation proposals

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
